title: Emergency Procedures Quiz
description: Test your knowledge of emergency procedures, distress communications, ELTs, and survival techniques from AIM Chapter 6

questions.question: According to 14 CFR 91.3, who is the final authority for the operation of the aircraft?
questions.explanation: The pilot-in-command is directly responsible for and is the final authority as to the operation of that aircraft. In an emergency, the PIC may deviate from any rule to meet that emergency.

questions.question: What must a pilot do after using emergency authority to deviate from an ATC clearance?
options: Notify ATC as soon as possible and obtain an amended clearance
Land at the nearest suitable airport
questions.explanation: If emergency authority is used to deviate from an ATC clearance, the pilot must notify ATC as soon as possible and obtain an amended clearance.

questions.question: What are the two types of emergency conditions?
questions.explanation: Emergency conditions are: Distress (immediate danger, requires immediate assistance) and Urgency (concerns safety but does not require immediate assistance).

questions.question: When should a pilot declare an emergency?
options: Only when the aircraft is on fire
When doubtful about position, fuel, weather, or any condition affecting safety
Only when structural damage has occurred
questions.explanation: Pilots should declare an emergency when doubtful about position, fuel endurance, weather, or any other condition that could adversely affect flight safety. Don't hesitate - ask for help!

questions.question: What is the international distress voice call?
questions.explanation: MAYDAY (said three times) is the international distress call indicating the aircraft is threatened by serious and/or imminent danger and requires immediate assistance.

questions.question: What is the urgency voice call?
questions.explanation: PAN-PAN (said three times) is the international urgency signal indicating the aircraft has an urgent message concerning safety but is not in immediate danger.

questions.question: What transponder code should be squawked during an emergency?
questions.explanation: Squawk 7700 for emergencies. This code triggers special indicators on radar displays. Continue squawking 7700 even if not yet in radar contact.

questions.question: What does squawk code 7500 indicate?
questions.explanation: Squawk 7500 indicates hijacking or unlawful interference. ATC will respond without requiring verbal confirmation to avoid alerting the hijacker.

questions.question: What is the international emergency frequency?
questions.explanation: 121.5 MHz is the international emergency (guard) Frequency. Most ATC facilities and aircraft monitor this frequency. ELTs also transmit on 121.5 MHz.

questions.question: What frequencies do modern 406 MHz ELTs transmit on?
questions.explanation: 406 MHz ELTs transmit on 406 MHz for satellite detection and also include a low-power 121.5 MHz homing transmitter for locating the aircraft.

questions.question: Why are 406 MHz ELTs preferred over 121.5 MHz ELTs?
options: Satellite monitoring, digital encoding with registration data, more accurate location
questions.explanation: 406 MHz ELTs are monitored by Cospas-Sarsat satellites (121.5 is no longer satellite-monitored), can be encoded with owner data, provide more accurate position, and enable faster rescue.

questions.question: With whom should 406 MHz ELTs be registered?
questions.explanation: 406 MHz ELTs must be registered with NOAA, which maintains the US registration database. This enables SAR to contact the owner and avoid false alarms.

questions.question: What should a VFR pilot do if inadvertently entering IMC?
options: Declare emergency, get radar assistance, or reverse course to VFR if possible
questions.explanation: AVFR pilot in IMC should declare a distress condition, state lack of instrument rating if applicable, and request radar vectors to VFR or an IFR clearance if rated/equipped.

questions.question: What information should be included in a MAYDAY call?
options: MAYDAY (3x), callsign, nature of distress, intentions, position, altitude, fuel, souls on board
questions.explanation: MAYDAY call should include: MAYDAY (3x), callsign, nature of distress, intentions/request, present position, altitude, fuel remaining, and number of souls aboard.

questions.question: What is the Air Force Rescue Coordination Center (AFRCC)?
options: The agency responsible for coordinating search and rescue for inland US
questions.explanation: AFRCC coordinates search and rescue for the inland US. The Coast Guard coordinates SAR for maritime areas. Both receive 406 MHz ELT alerts from NOAA.

questions.question: When does search and rescue begin for an overdue aircraft with a flight plan?
options: 30 minutes after ETA, no contact, and failed communication attempts
questions.explanation: SAR begins when: (1) Information suggests aircraft is missing, (2) Aircraft is overdue 30 minutes and communications are unsuccessful, or (3) ELT signal is received.

questions.question: What light gun signal means 'cleared to land' for aircraft in flight?
questions.explanation: Steady green to aircraft in flight means 'Cleared to land.' Flashing green means 'Return for landing.'

questions.question: What should you do if you see steady red light signals while in flight?
options: Continue circling and give way to other aircraft
questions.explanation: Steady red to aircraft in flight means 'Give way to other aircraft and continue circling.' The airport may be unsafe for landing.

questions.question: What emergency equipment should pilots have for flights over uninhabited areas?
options: Survival equipment appropriate to terrain (food, water, shelter, signaling)
questions.explanation: For flights over uninhabited areas, carry survival equipment appropriate to the terrain: water, food, shelter material, signaling devices, first aid kit, etc.

questions.question: What does MSAW alert controllers about?
questions.explanation: MSAW (Minimum Safe Altitude Warning) alerts controllers when Mode C-equipped aircraft under their control are at or below a predetermined minimum safe altitude.

questions.question: Can ATC clear pilots through hazardous weather?
options: No, pilots must deviate when necessary for safety
questions.explanation: The pilot is the final authority. ATC assistance is advisory only. If hazardous weather is encountered, pilots should take immediate action to avoid it, even if deviating from clearance.

questions.question: What is the DF (Direction Finding) steer?
options: Radar vectors based on aircraft radio transmission
questions.explanation: DF (Direction Finding) is a service where ATC can determine aircraft bearing based on radio transmissions and provide heading guidance to an airport.

questions.question: How should a pilot acknowledge tower light gun signals during the day?
questions.explanation: During daylight, acknowledge light signals by rocking wings. At night, acknowledge by flashing landing lights or navigation lights.

questions.question: What action should be taken if you experience an engine fire in flight?
options: Follow POH procedures: mixture cutoff, fuel shutoff, master off, emergency descent/landing
questions.explanation: For engine fire: follow POH emergency procedures immediately - typically mixture cutoff, fuel shutoff, attempt to extinguish, land ASAP. Declare emergency!

questions.question: What is the 'Pilot's Discretion' aspect of emergency authority?
options: Pilot can deviate from any rule to meet an emergency, but must be able to justify decisions
questions.explanation: In an emergency, PIC may deviate from any rule to the extent necessary. However, if requested, a written report may be required. Good judgment must be used.
